newsitem.title: USA: CME Nov lumber ends limit up on cash gains, rumors.
newsitem.headline: CME Nov lumber ends limit up on cash gains, rumors.

text.p: November CME lumber futures closed up the daily $10 per thousand board foot (tbf) daily limit and other months ended mostly higher on demand linked to rising cash prices and rumors that some Canadian mills may have reached yearly export quotas ahead of time, traders said.
November closed limit up at $398.70 per tbf and January finished $5.40 higher at $400.40 after setting a new high of $401.80 earlier. Other months ended up $2.00 to off $0.40.
"Increased rumors, relative to the quota, continued to lead to speculative buying" in futures, said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney forest products analyst.
Schmaedick noted that the talk over Canadian mills reaching their quota was boosting cash lumber prices.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce up $10 per tbf at $388 compared with a week ago. Cash sources are now saying prices may have exceeded $400 in Friday's trade, traders said.
Futures trading was uneven early on profit taking ahead of Thursday's U.S. housing starts report before rallying on fresh demand and buy stops, they said.
Early estimates on the September housing report averaged 1.47 million units in a range of 1.43 million to 1.50 million and compared with 1.525 million starts in August.
